acceptance.given: The declared A24 integration case and shared helper have been authored and frozen, and the real validator entry is available through the owning execution protocol.

oracle.expected: The integration invocation uses a literal argv list headed by the active Python interpreter, followed by -B and scripts/sc/validate_skill_quality.py with the published repository-root, policy, skill-root and mode arguments; shell is explicitly False, cwd resolves to the repository root, and timeout is finite and positive.
forbidden: A shell command string replaces the literal argv list.
shell=True or an implicit shell setting is used.
Repository cwd is omitted or resolves elsewhere.
Timeout is omitted, None, nonpositive or nonfinite.
A mocked subprocess result substitutes for execution of the published CLI.
oracle.observable: During pre-RED inspection of test_a24 and its frozen helper, inspect the subprocess call construction; during A24 execution, observe the actual arguments and keyword arguments through instrumentation that delegates to the real subprocess call. Check the invocation boundary independently of CLI return values.

acceptance.then: The terminal integration invocation satisfies all four declared process-boundary checks.
acceptance.when: The A24 integration test is inspected before formal RED and subsequently invokes the published CLI during targeted and whole-plan terminal validation.

failure_intents.selector_intent: In scripts/sc/tests/test_skill_quality_migration.py::test_a24, assert the literal argv construction, explicit shell=False, repository cwd and finite positive subprocess timeout while delegating to the actual scripts/sc/validate_skill_quality.py CLI. The case also directly calls scripts.sc.validate_skill_quality.validate_package or main for production-entry binding. A boundary violation must produce an observable AssertionError under the targeted pytest command with a 300-second caller timeout. Missing imports, missing planned tests, environment failures and timeouts are blockers or harness failures, never causal product RED.
